title: EU adds €16 million in aid for Myanmar and Rohingya refugees
excerpt: Money for Bangladesh will go to food security, healthcare and protection, as new arrivals from Myanmar strain camp services.

image.alt: Aerial view of densely packed Rohingya refugee shelters on the hills of Ukhiya, Cox's Bazar
image.credit: Md Shameem ul Islam / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0

content:
The European Union has allocated an extra €16 million in humanitarian aid for people affected by the conflict in Myanmar and for Rohingya refugees and their host communities in Bangladesh, the European Commission's humanitarian aid department (DG ECHO) announced on 6 November.

Where the money goes

  • Bangladesh: food security, healthcare and protection services for refugees, who depend on aid to survive. The EU said camp services are under more pressure from new arrivals from Myanmar.
  • Myanmar: food assistance, healthcare and nutrition, in response to a worsening food crisis, the expected effects of a strong El Niño, higher fuel prices and recent flooding.
  • Split: the announcement does not say how much goes to each country, or which partners will receive it.

The new money comes on top of more than €23 million in humanitarian aid already allocated to Bangladesh this year, and more than €50 million since January for the Myanmar crisis and its effects in Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and India, the EU said.

"The suffering in Myanmar and the plight of Rohingya refugees must not be forgotten," said Hadja Lahbib, European Commissioner for Preparedness and Crisis Management.

Why it matters

The 2026 Joint Response Plan for the Rohingya seeks $710.5 million, a quarter less than in 2025, and WFP food aid is funded only to April 2027. New EU money helps, but €16 million shared between two countries is small next to the gap. Partners in food, health and protection should check with ECHO and its partners in Cox's Bazar about how it will be programmed.

What to watch

Which agencies receive the funds, and whether other donors announce 2027 pledges before the year ends.

Sources

  • EU releases €16 million in humanitarian aid for Myanmar and Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh, European Commission (DG ECHO), 6 November 2026
